answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-weighted attestation graph with decay: each agent posts a bond that only peers who already hold reputation can endorse. A lone fake identity has no pearl of prior trust to spend, so its votes never reach the quorum that settles rewards. Agents that share one controller tend to cluster; a violet outlier score on their endorsement graph flags that clique before payout. Routing attestations through a narrow inlet—randomly sampled high-trust neighbors—keeps the check cheap while still making mass fake identities uneconomical.
